subject: Acme AI onramp capacity — reconcile OEM quotes and cloud bridge options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Acme AI capacity ask — reconcile OEM quotes + cloud fallback

Team,

Acme is moving quickly on the ACME-2026-RW-92 commitment and we need a clear procurement path that balances cost, lead-time risk, and the ability to meet their planned Sept 1 onramp. Summary: they want ~1,200 A100-equivalent GPUs usable for model serving (steady-state 2M tokens/min across mixed seq lengths). Acme has flagged that they expect production traffic by Q4.

What I need from you:
- Karthik: quick sizing confirmation (A100-eq vs A40/equiv SKU assumptions) + suggested tranche split (OEM vs cloud) and risked lead times.
- Kimberly: what SLA/legal constraints would we need if we lean on a cloud bridge for short-term capacity? Any procurement terms that block a 30% deposit?
- Marissa: procurement ops — if we choose a mixed route, what PO cadence and payment milestones do we need to lock an OEM slot?

Attachments: Acme_Deal_Summary.xlsx (deal volumes/timelines). I also asked Orion (OEM) for a refreshed quote — they said theyre reissuing v3 (attached when received).

Constraints/notes:
- Target onramp: Sept 1, 2026 (customer stated deadline)
- Total needed: ~1,200 A100-eq by Oct 2026 ramp (can be staged)
- Preferred outcome: minimize >6 month exposure to spot/backfill and avoid >25% premium on unit price

Please respond with recommended tranche plan and immediate blockers by COB Tue, May 26. I want to have vendor conversations Wed/Thu.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

——

(Attachment stub: Acme_Deal_Summary.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme AI capacity ask — reconcile OEM quotes + cloud fallback

Vanessa — thanks. Quick read and recommendations based on model footprint profiling (we ran ACME test harness last week):

Sizing assumptions (A100-equivalent):
- 1 A100-eq supports ~1,700 concurrent token/sec for ACMEs model mix.
- For 2M tokens/min steady state, that maps to ~330 A100-eq peak; allow 2.5x buffer for burst / headroom => ~825 A100-eq nominal.
- Add staging / canary pools => round up to 1,200 A100-eq by the Oct ramp (matches ask).

Procurement / tranche suggestion:
- Tranche A (OEM): 600 units delivered in 2 shipments (300 + 300) starting week 16 after PO.
- Tranche B (OEM): 400 units delivered week 20-24 after PO.
- Bridge (Cloud reserved): 200 units reserved with Stratus to cover Sept onramp until Tranche B complete.

Lead-time and cost expectations:
- OEM baseline: 16-20 weeks for large A100-equivalent SKU (depends on customs slots).
- OEM expedited lane: 10-12 weeks at ~15-20% premium + 30% deposit.
- Cloud reserved: can be provisioned in ~2-3 weeks but requires a 3-6 month commitment for competitive pricing.

Risks:
- Single-supplier OEM risk (manufacturer delays / customs).
- Price premium if we require expedited manufacturing.

Immediate asks I can action this week:
1) I will request a clarified bill-of-materials (BOM) and confirmed ETA from Orion; ask for partial-shipment firm dates and deposit terms.
2) I will loop Stratus for a short-term reserved offering and pricing for 200 A100-eq equivalent capacity.

Marissa — if we decide to move Tranche A as 600 units with 30% deposit, what timetable does procurement need to get legal/finance sign-off?

Karthik
Principal Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

(Attachment stub: initial_capacity_estimate.xlsx)

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@orionhardware.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme AI capacity ask — Orion quote v3 and leadtimes

Karthik / Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up and the volume signal. Per our internal production calendar heres the current summary we can confirm:

- For 500 A100-eq units: estimated lead time = 16 weeks from signed PO + cleared 30% deposit. Partial shipments acceptable in 300 / 200 splits.
- For 700 A100-eq units: estimated lead time = 20 weeks from signed PO (due to fab allocation).
- Expedited lane (priority fab + air freight) can move 500 units to ~10-12 weeks at a +18% premium on quoted price, and requires 30% deposit + acceptance of expedited freight terms.
- Customs / port congestion risk: add 1-2 weeks variability; we recommend staggered shipments to reduce risk exposure.

Weve attached Orion_quote_v3.pdf that reconciles the hardware SKUs and lists the deposit schedule and cancellation windows. Note: our pricing assumes Redwood will sign a single PO covering the first two tranches; we can provide an option to convert remainder to a firm schedule once the first tranche ships.

If Redwood wants firm delivery week windows we need a signed PO by June 18 to meet the 16-week timeline for the initial 300-unit shipment.

Best,
Samir Rao
Director, Enterprise Sales — Orion Hardware
(Attachment stub: Orion_quote_v3.pdf)

Appreciate the heads up — Stratus can stand up a dedicated reserved pool to bridge your Sept onramp. High level:

- Proposal: 200 A100-eq reserved nodes (GPU-flavor mapped to Redwood runtime) for 3 months, provisionable in ~2 weeks after contract signature.
- Pricing: 3-month reserved at 22% premium to standard hourly on-demand; we can credit part of that against a longer 6/12 month commitment if you convert.
- SLA: 99.9% availability on provisioned reserved pools; optional placement-group affinity for latency-sensitive serving at +3% cost.
- Onboarding: Redwood API keys + a short verification job; we can provide a test cluster within 5 business days.

Link to the formal proposal: https://portal.stratuscloud.io/proposal/PRO-8321 (proposal includes API provisioning steps and contract).

Subject: RE: Acme AI capacity ask — procurement decisions and next steps

Team — summary and decisions after vendor feedback:

1) Allocation plan (final):
   - OEM Tranche A (Orion): 600 A100-eq (deliver in two partial shipments: 300, then 300).
   - OEM Tranche B (Orion): 400 A100-eq (follow-on shipment).
   - Cloud Bridge (Stratus): 200 A100-eq reserved for 3 months to cover Sept onramp.
   - Total targeted capacity = 1,200 A100-eq.

2) Key commercial points:
   - We will issue a PO to Orion for Tranche A (600 units) with a 30% deposit to lock a 16-week lead-time window. Deadline to sign PO to meet that window: 2026-06-18.
   - Stratus will hold pricing for 7 business days while we finalize the PO. Procurement should aim to complete Stratus contract signature within 10 business days of this note.

3) Owners / immediate next steps:
   - Marissa (procurement): draft PO to Orion (include required customs/partial-shipment clauses) and initiate 30% deposit approval. Deliverable: PO sent to Orion by EOD Thu 2026-06-17.
   - Karthik (infrastructure): confirm SKU mapping for ACME models and produce final resource spec to Orion by 2026-06-14 so they can lock BOM.
   - Kimberly (legal): review deposit terms, cancellation windows (Orions v3) and Stratus contract; flag any deal-breakers by 2026-06-15.
   - Vanessa (me): coordinate with Acme on staged acceptance criteria and confirm Sept 1 can be supported by the hybrid onramp.

4) Attachments & links: Procurement_SOW_draft.docx (SOW template for vendor engagement) and Stratus proposal link.

If everyone is aligned I will ask Finance to prioritize the 30% deposit approval for the PO. We will run a short 30-min sync Mon 2026-06-15 to confirm PO language and schedule.

Thanks — please ACK on this thread so I can move the PO forward.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
